claims.text: The first Harambee Prosperity Plan (HPP) was introduced in 2016 under President Hage Geingob. It sought faster progress against poverty and large inequalities in wealth, supporting the longer national development direction. Its five pillars joined effective governance and service delivery, economic advancement, social progression, infrastructure development, and international relations and cooperation. Governance concerns accountable decisions and useful services. Economic advancement concerns productive opportunities and employment. Social progression includes food security, housing, sanitation and skills. Infrastructure supplies networks such as water, electricity and transport. International cooperation links national action with regional and wider partners. These are the plan’s intended contributions, not five proven achievements. Keep this 2016 example distinct from later plans.
